factions.name: Galactic Republic
factions.label: GALACTIC REPUBLIC
factions.text: A union of member worlds governed through the Senate. In the High Republic it reaches toward the frontier; centuries later, institutional weakness and a manufactured war make it vulnerable to Palpatine.
factions.reading: Follow the gold stream into the Clone Wars. Its split marks secession; its abrupt change to red marks the conversion of republican institutions into the Empire.

factions.name: Rebel cells → Rebel Alliance
factions.label: REBEL ALLIANCE
factions.text: Resistance begins in scattered networks. Mon Mothma helps bring rebel cells together into an alliance; military victories then give that movement the capacity to establish a government.
factions.reading: The thread begins as early opposition, not a formally founded Alliance. It broadens toward Yavin and Endor, then becomes the New Republic.

factions.name: New Republic
factions.label: NEW REPUBLIC
factions.text: The victorious rebellion builds a Senate and civilian government. The Galactic Concordance ends the main war, while disarmament and political division leave the Republic poorly prepared for the First Order.
factions.reading: This government grows from the Alliance after Endor. Its institutional stream collapses at Hosnian Prime; that does not mean every member world disappears.

factions.name: Resistance & allied uprising
factions.label: RESISTANCE
factions.text: Leia organizes a small force to oppose the First Order. It survives devastating defeats and becomes the nucleus around which a much larger civilian fleet and galactic uprising gather.
factions.reading: The movement branches from the New Republic period but is not its regular army. Its final widening includes independent allies, not a newly established galactic government.

factions.name: Galactic Empire
factions.label: GALACTIC EMPIRE
factions.text: Palpatine turns the Republic into an authoritarian state, retaining its administrative machinery and imposing military control. Planetary terror and political repression provoke the rebellion that eventually breaks its central power.
factions.reading: The red stream inherits the Republic and conquered Separatist space. Endor fractures central rule; Jakku leaves scattered remnants rather than erasing every Imperial force.

factions.name: Imperial remnants
factions.label: IMPERIAL REMNANTS
factions.text: Defeat leaves surviving warlords, loyalists, and clandestine networks. Some remain in known space while others build strength in the Unknown Regions.
factions.reading: This is an aggregate of separate forces. The transition into the First Order is selective and schematic; it does not claim every remnant joined it, or assign one exact founding date.

factions.name: First Order
factions.label: FIRST ORDER
factions.text: An Imperial successor built in secrecy becomes an open conquering power. The destruction of the New Republic capital allows the First Order to rapidly expand its reach.
factions.reading: Its early boundary is approximate: the organization develops over years. A related Sith fleet appears alongside it at the end; the two are not the same institution.

factions.name: Sith Eternal fleet
factions.label: SITH ETERNAL
factions.text: On Exegol, Palpatine’s cult secretly builds the fleet intended to enforce a new Sith empire. Its public emergence culminates in the Battle of Exegol.
factions.reading: The political ribbon shows the fleet’s emergence at 35 ABY, not the foundation of the cult. Its longer hidden continuity is represented in the separate Sith track.

factions.name: Separatist Alliance
factions.label: SEPARATISTS
factions.text: The Confederacy of Independent Systems breaks from the Republic. Its droid armies fight the Clone Wars, while its leadership is manipulated by the same Sith conspiracy that controls its opponent.
factions.reading: This stream pulls away from the Republic, then ends when its leadership is eliminated and the Empire absorbs its power base.

factions.name: The Nihil
factions.label: NIHIL
factions.text: Marauders challenge Republic expansion with terror attacks and control over hyperspace travel. The destruction of Starlight Beacon and the Occlusion Zone turn a frontier threat into a major crisis.
factions.reading: The ribbon highlights the height of the Nihil crisis. Its taper is schematic and does not assert that every Nihil faction vanished on a single date.

factions.name: Independent worlds & regional powers
factions.label: INDEPENDENT WORLDS
factions.text: The galaxy contains societies beyond the reach of its largest states: independent systems, Mandalorian factions, Hutt interests, criminal networks, and other regional powers. Their relationships change throughout the saga.
factions.reading: This grouping is a cartographic simplification, not a single faction or alliance. It also leaves room for the limits of central government and gaps in the story.

factions.name: The Jedi tradition
factions.text: From public peacekeepers to hunted survivors, then Luke’s students and Rey, the Jedi thread shows a tradition enduring institutional destruction.
factions.reading: This separate track represents continuity and visibility, not political territory or a count of Jedi. Its narrow surviving line after Order 66 matters as much as its earlier breadth.

factions.name: The Sith tradition
factions.text: Hidden Sith plotting culminates in Sidious’s Empire. After Endor, Palpatine and the Sith Eternal continue in secret on Exegol.
factions.reading: This is a tradition and conspiracy track, not a population measure. The First Order’s dark-side users are not automatically classified as Sith.

events.title: An expanding frontier
events.text: Jedi and Republic explorers reach farther into the Outer Rim. The Path of the Open Hand challenges the Jedi’s relationship with the Force.
events.effect: Expansion brings the Republic into contact and conflict with worlds beyond its established reach.

events.title: The Great Disaster
events.text: A hyperspace catastrophe threatens inhabited systems. Jedi coordinate a vast rescue as the Nihil emerge as a dangerous opponent.
events.effect: The Republic’s optimistic expansion meets a threat that exploits the routes binding the galaxy together.

events.title: Starlight shines
events.text: Starlight Beacon opens as a Republic outpost and symbol of connection between the Core and frontier.
events.effect: A public investment in unity also creates a conspicuous target.

events.title: Starlight falls
events.text: The Nihil sabotage Starlight Beacon above Eiram. The station’s destruction strikes at both the Jedi and the Republic’s promise of protection.
events.effect: The frontier crisis deepens. The Nihil’s subsequent Occlusion Zone cuts worlds off from Republic access.

events.title: A shadow in the Force
events.text: Murders draw Jedi into an investigation that exposes concealed failures and a dark-side threat.
events.effect: The map’s hidden Sith thread continues alongside a still-powerful Jedi institution.
events.note: The story reveals a hidden threat; it is not the public return of the Sith recognized by the Jedi Council.

events.title: The Naboo crisis
events.text: The Trade Federation invades Naboo. Palpatine rises to the chancellorship while Darth Maul’s appearance reveals that the Sith have returned.
events.effect: A local crisis becomes a decisive shift in the leadership of the Republic.

events.title: The Separatist break
events.text: Dooku’s secession movement draws worlds away from the Republic, preparing the political division that becomes the Clone Wars.
events.effect: A new political stream branches from the Republic before open war begins.
events.note: Placed around 24 BBY to show the developing movement; secession was a process, not one simultaneous departure.

events.title: The Clone Wars begin
events.text: Republic clones and Separatist droids clash at Geonosis. The Jedi become military commanders in a war whose opposing leaders are being manipulated by Sidious.
events.effect: The Republic divides into rival war machines while emergency power accumulates around its Chancellor.

events.title: The Siege of Mandalore
events.text: Ahsoka and allied Mandalorians confront Maul as the Clone Wars reach their final days.
events.effect: Mandalore’s internal conflicts intersect with the collapse of the Republic, showing why regional histories do not fit neatly into two sides.

events.title: Order 66
events.text: Palpatine turns the clone army against the Jedi. Anakin joins the Sith as Darth Vader, and survivors of the purge are driven into hiding.
events.effect: The Jedi institution collapses almost overnight. Its surviving tradition remains as a thin, continuous thread.

events.title: The Empire is declared
events.text: Palpatine reorganizes the Republic into the Galactic Empire. Separatist leaders are killed and their power base is absorbed into the new order.
events.effect: Gold becomes red: this is a takeover of the existing state, not the arrival of a foreign civilization.

events.title: Life at the margins
events.text: Han Solo’s early adventures move through Imperial recruitment, exploited frontier worlds, and powerful crime syndicates.
events.effect: The independent-worlds band includes criminal and regional power that coexists with Imperial rule.

events.title: Jedi in hiding
events.text: Obi-Wan emerges from exile to protect Leia and confronts Vader. The Inquisitors continue hunting survivors.
events.effect: The Jedi thread is diminished, but knowledge and personal connections survive the purge.

events.title: The sparks of rebellion
events.text: Local resistance, covert organizers, and emerging rebel cells begin to connect. Cassian Andor and the Ghost crew inhabit different parts of this growing opposition.
events.effect: Scattered acts of resistance gradually become an organized challenge.

events.title: The Alliance unites
events.text: After condemning Imperial violence, Mon Mothma escapes arrest and calls for rebel cells to unite.
events.effect: Separate networks coalesce into a shared political and military movement.

events.title: The sacrifice at Scarif
events.text: Rogue One secures and transmits the Death Star plans at the cost of the team’s lives.
events.effect: A local operation creates the possibility of defeating the Empire’s greatest weapon.
media: Rogue One · A Star Wars Story

events.title: Alderaan destroyed
events.text: The Death Star destroys Alderaan in a demonstration of Imperial terror.
events.effect: The regime’s promise of absolute control is made brutally visible.

events.title: The Battle of Yavin
events.text: Luke Skywalker destroys the first Death Star, saving the rebel base and demonstrating that the Empire can be defeated.
events.effect: The rebellion gains a defining victory. This battle is the reference point for BBY and ABY dates.

events.title: The retreat from Hoth
events.text: Imperial forces drive the rebels from Echo Base. The Alliance survives by dispersing rather than defending one fixed capital.
events.effect: Rebel influence dips without ending the movement’s continuity.

events.title: The Battle of Endor
events.text: The second Death Star is destroyed. Vader turns against Palpatine to save Luke, and Imperial central authority begins to break apart.
events.effect: The Empire fractures into remnants while the victorious rebellion moves toward government.

events.title: A Republic rebuilt
events.text: The Alliance gives way to a new republican government and a restored Senate.
events.effect: A resistance movement becomes a state, while the wider war continues.

events.title: Jakku & the Concordance
events.text: The Empire’s last major stand ends at Jakku. The Galactic Concordance formalizes peace between the New Republic and the defeated Imperial state.
events.effect: The main war ends. Remnants and hidden networks persist beyond the treaty.

events.title: A fragile peace
events.text: Imperial warlords and secret projects endure while the New Republic works to consolidate peace. Din Djarin and Grogu travel through this unsettled galaxy.
events.effect: The map keeps a remnant stream alive: Endor and Jakku were not the end of every Imperial organization.
events.note: Around 9 ABY marks the beginning of this screen-story period. Later connected series are not all assigned this exact year.

events.title: Leia forms the Resistance
events.text: Leia builds an independent force to investigate and resist the First Order as many New Republic leaders underestimate the danger.
events.effect: A small opposition stream branches within the New Republic era.

events.title: Luke’s temple falls
events.text: Luke’s attempt to restore the Jedi ends in catastrophe as Ben Solo falls to the dark side. Luke withdraws to Ahch-To.
events.effect: The renewed institution collapses; the Jedi legacy survives outside its walls.

events.title: Hosnian Prime destroyed
events.text: Starkiller Base annihilates the Hosnian system, destroying the New Republic’s capital and central leadership.
events.effect: The First Order exploits the institutional collapse to launch its conquest.

events.title: Starkiller Base falls
events.text: The Resistance destroys Starkiller Base, but the wider First Order military remains capable of pursuing its enemies.
events.effect: Destroying a superweapon does not by itself reverse the collapse of the Republic.

events.title: The last stand on Crait
events.text: Luke’s final intervention gives the surviving Resistance time to escape. Rey carries the Jedi texts into an uncertain future.
events.effect: The Resistance contracts to a handful of survivors, while a renewed Jedi thread continues through Rey.

events.title: The hidden fleet emerges
events.text: Palpatine reveals the forces assembled by the Sith Eternal on Exegol and seeks to combine them with the First Order.
events.effect: A separate military stream emerges from the long-hidden Sith conspiracy.

events.title: Exegol & the uprising
events.text: Rey confronts Palpatine while the Resistance and a vast civilian fleet attack the Sith Eternal. The victory accompanies uprisings against First Order rule across the galaxy.
events.effect: Centralized conquest breaks down. The map ends with allied resistance and liberated worlds, without inventing the government that follows.

screen.name: Young Jedi Adventures
screen.note: High Republic placement, around 232 BBY. The marker does not claim every season occupies a single year.

screen.name: The Acolyte
screen.note: Main investigation. The Brendok flashback is earlier, around 148 BBY.

screen.name: The Clone Wars
screen.note: The main wartime narrative. The final arc overlaps Revenge of the Sith; the closing Imperial-era coda is outside this span.

screen.name: The Bad Batch
screen.note: Main story in the early Imperial period. The later Omega epilogue is not treated as continuous screen time.

screen.name: Maul – Shadow Lord
screen.note: Early Imperial era, approximately 18 BBY. Sources differ on the exact placement; this is an approximate marker, not a precise duration.

screen.name: Solo
screen.note: Includes the Corellia opening and the three-year jump to the principal adventure. The bracket includes the intervening gap.

screen.name: Obi-Wan Kenobi
screen.note: Main story, excluding the prequel-era opening and flashbacks.

screen.name: Andor · seasons 1–2
screen.note: Main story across the two seasons. Season 2 advances in year-separated arcs and ends immediately before Rogue One. Childhood flashbacks sit outside this span.

screen.name: Rebels
screen.note: The main rebellion narrative runs alongside Andor. Later epilogue scenes are not included in this continuous span.

screen.name: Rogue One
screen.note: Main mission, immediately before A New Hope. The childhood opening is earlier.

screen.name: IV · A New Hope
screen.note: Contains the Battle of Yavin, the BBY/ABY reference point.

screen.name: The Mandalorian
screen.note: Begins around 9 ABY. Later-season elapsed time is not securely fixed here. This marks the shared New Republic story period, not an assertion that all three seasons last one year.

screen.name: The Book of Boba Fett
screen.note: Main present-day story in the Mandalorian period. Flashbacks begin after Return of the Jedi, around 4 ABY.

screen.name: Ahsoka · season 1
screen.note: Placed in the shared New Republic period, conventionally around 9 ABY. The precise ordering and elapsed time among related series are not implied by the stacked labels.

screen.name: Skeleton Crew
screen.note: Around 9 ABY, in the same broad New Republic period as the Mandalorian stories. Same-year placement does not prove scene-by-scene simultaneity.

screen.name: The Mandalorian and Grogu
screen.note: After the Mandalorian series, within the New Republic era. This shared-era anchor is approximate; the exact in-universe year and duration are not asserted.

screen.name: Resistance
screen.note: Begins before The Force Awakens and continues beyond it. The show overlaps the sequel conflict.

screen.name: VIII · The Last Jedi
screen.note: Begins immediately after The Force Awakens.

screen.name: Tales of the Jedi
screen.note: An approximate anthology envelope from Dooku’s earlier career to Ahsoka after the purge. Separate episodes and time jumps, not a continuously unfolding 50-year story.

screen.name: Tales of the Empire
screen.note: Disconnected Morgan Elsbeth and Barriss Offee stories, from the Clone Wars into the New Republic era. Exact endpoints and individual episode dates vary.

undatedScreen.name: Tales of the Underworld
undatedScreen.note: Cad Bane and Asajj Ventress stories occupy separate periods. The broad chronology is known, but no single reliable continuous span is drawn here.

undatedScreen.name: Forces of Destiny
undatedScreen.note: Short stories scattered across several eras. They are not represented as one continuous range.

undatedScreen.name: Visions & LEGO stories
undatedScreen.note: Separate storytelling continuities; not plotted as canonical history or silently substituted for Legends.

ancient.name: Legends · ancient past
ancient.intro: Expanded Universe versions of the distant past. Canon also names ancient eras and some events; these particular accounts remain Legends and are not missing chapters of Disney canon.

events.title: Dawn of the Jedi
events.text: On Tython, the Je’daii confront the Rakatan threat in the ancient Expanded Universe.
events.effect: A distinct Legends account of Force traditions before the familiar Jedi Order.

events.title: The Force War
events.text: The Tython conflict reaches its culmination in the Dawn of the Jedi comics.
events.effect: The chart follows the Legends tradition into the later Jedi; it does not claim canon’s Jedi origin is identical.
media: Dawn of the Jedi: Force War

events.title: The Great Hyperspace War
events.text: Naga Sadow’s Sith Empire attacks the Republic in the Tales of the Jedi account.
events.effect: A major collision between an established Republic and an external Sith empire.

events.title: The Great Sith War
events.text: Exar Kun and Ulic Qel-Droma’s war reaches its climax, drawing Jedi, Sith, and Mandalorians into a galactic conflict.
events.effect: The Sith threat grows through fallen Jedi as well as rival states.

events.title: Revan & the Jedi Civil War
events.text: The Republic and Jedi struggle against a Sith war machine in Knights of the Old Republic.
events.effect: An alternate-continuity story of allegiance, identity, and competing galactic powers.
media: Knights of the Old Republic · game

events.title: The Jedi Exile
events.text: The Sith Lords follows the Jedi Exile through a galaxy where the Jedi have been driven close to extinction.
events.effect: The Jedi tradition narrows while the conflict continues through hidden adversaries.
media: Knights of the Old Republic II · game

events.title: The Old Republic
events.text: A resurgent Sith Empire contests the Republic; later expansions bring additional powers into the struggle.
events.effect: The wide Sith/rival-empires band aggregates changing antagonists rather than presenting them as one unchanging state.
media: The Old Republic · game and expansions

events.title: The New Sith Wars
events.text: A long sequence of Jedi–Sith conflicts begins in the Legends chronology.
events.effect: The timeline compresses a millennium of changing factions and warfare.

events.title: Ruusan & Darth Bane
events.text: The New Sith Wars end near Ruusan. Bane’s Rule of Two replaces the massed Sith orders in the Legends account.
events.effect: A broad Sith presence becomes a hidden lineage. The section stops here and does not splice itself into the canon Republic.

future.name: Legends · distant future
future.intro: The later Expanded Universe continues its own post-Endor history. This is not what happens after Exegol: it follows a different timeline, including an earlier Yuuzhan Vong war and a different Skywalker family.

events.title: The Dark Nest aftermath
events.text: The final phase of the Killik conflict reshapes the Jedi’s relationships and leadership.
events.effect: This 36 ABY entry continues a Legends crisis that began in 35 ABY; it does not follow the canon sequel trilogy.

events.title: Legacy of the Force
events.text: Jacen Solo’s fall and a new civil war divide the Galactic Alliance and the Skywalker–Solo family.
events.effect: A different family history and political order make the continuity break explicit.

events.title: The war’s reckoning
events.text: The conflict around Darth Caedus reaches its conclusion.
events.effect: The end of one Sith ruler does not erase the institutional damage left by the civil war.

events.title: Fate of the Jedi
events.text: Luke and Ben Skywalker’s journey intersects with threats to the Jedi and the Galactic Alliance.
events.effect: The Jedi remain an institution with a history distinct from Luke’s failed canon academy.

events.title: Crucible
events.text: Luke, Han, and Leia face another crisis in the later Legends novel timeline.
events.effect: The familiar heroes’ story extends well beyond their different canon trajectories.

events.title: The Legacy era
events.text: Cade Skywalker’s era finds an Imperial order contested by the One Sith, surviving Jedi, and other galactic forces.
events.effect: This is the comic-book future of Legends, not a forecast of upcoming canon stories.

events.title: A new galactic balance
events.text: Later Legacy stories follow the continuing struggle after Darth Krayt’s reign.
events.effect: The chart extends toward 140 ABY as a schematic of the later comic era, without inventing detailed history for the intervening decades.

lifelines.name: Anakin Skywalker / Darth Vader
lifelines.note: The same person across the Republic and Imperial eras. The line ends with his death at Endor; his later presence as a Force spirit is not an extension of his physical life.

lifelines.name: Padmé Amidala
lifelines.note: Queen and then senator of Naboo. She dies after giving birth to Luke and Leia as the Republic becomes the Empire.

lifelines.name: Luke Skywalker
lifelines.note: Born at the fall of the Republic. His life ends on Ahch-To after his projection at Crait. Later appearances as a Force spirit fall outside this physical lifeline.

lifelines.name: Leia Organa
lifelines.note: Luke’s twin, a leader of the Rebellion and later the Resistance. She dies on Ajan Kloss after reaching out through the Force to Ben.

lifelines.name: Ben Solo / Kylo Ren
lifelines.note: The son of Han and Leia. His changing allegiance does not split his identity into separate lives. He dies after restoring Rey to life on Exegol.

lifelines.name: Rey Skywalker
lifelines.note: Alive at the end of The Rise of Skywalker. Her temporary death and revival at Exegol occur within the same year. The open endpoint leaves her later life uncharted. “Skywalkers” includes her chosen name, not a claim of biological descent.

lifelines.name: Yoda
lifelines.note: About 900 years old when he dies on Dagobah in 4 ABY, implying a birth around 896 BBY. His line enters from above the map’s 500 BBY boundary. Force-spirit appearances are excluded.

lifelines.name: Qui-Gon Jinn
lifelines.note: His canon birth is approximately 80 BBY. Maul kills him during the Battle of Naboo. The older Legends birth date is not used.

lifelines.name: Obi-Wan Kenobi
lifelines.note: Mentor to Anakin and Luke. This map uses the familiar Yavin-zero convention for A New Hope. Some newer reference chronologies label its pre-Yavin events 1 BBY. His physical life ends aboard the Death Star.

lifelines.name: Ahsoka Tano
lifelines.note: The open endpoint marks her New Republic story period, around 9 ABY, rather than a death. Precise dating of the connected series varies. Her temporary death and revival on Mortis do not end this lifeline.

lifelines.name: Din Grogu
lifelines.note: Approximately 50 years old when The Mandalorian begins, giving an approximate birth around 41 BBY. His open endpoint marks the broad New Republic screen-story period used here; it does not date his final appearance or predict his fate.

lifelines.name: Han Solo
lifelines.note: A Corellian smuggler who becomes a Rebel general. His line ends at Starkiller Base, where he is killed by his son Ben.

lifelines.name: Chewbacca
lifelines.note: A life spanning the late High Republic, the Empire, and the First Order conflict. He is alive after Exegol. His death in the alternate Legends continuity is not imported into this canon line.

lifelines.name: Lando Calrissian
lifelines.note: His approximate birth follows the age given in The Rise of Skywalker’s reference material; some earlier sources differ. He survives the Battle of Exegol, so the line ends with an open marker.

lifelines.name: Finn
lifelines.note: Born during the New Republic and raised by the First Order. He becomes a Resistance general and is alive after the Battle of Exegol.

lifelines.name: Poe Dameron
lifelines.note: Born during the Galactic Civil War. A Resistance pilot and later general, he is alive after the Battle of Exegol.
